books.title: Libellus de Medicinalibus Indorum Herbis
books.author: Martín de la Cruz
books.description: The only surviving Aztec herbal. 185 illustrated plant medicines with preparations, written in Nahuatl by a Tlatelolco physician and translated into Latin in 1552. The earliest illustrated herbal from the Americas, with hand-painted plant portraits by Aztec artists.

books.title: De Materia Medica
books.author: Pedanius Dioscorides
books.description: The foundational pharmacological text of Western medicine. 600 plants across 5 books, used continuously for 1,500 years.

books.title: Papyrus Ebers
books.author: Anonymous Egyptian physicians
books.description: The oldest and most complete ancient medical text. 700 remedies, 300 plant medicines, surgical procedures from 1550 BCE.

books.title: Charaka Samhita
books.author: Charaka
books.description: The foundational Ayurvedic text. 340 chapters covering pharmacology and the 8 branches of medicine. Documents plants 2,000 years before modern clinical validation.

books.title: Bencao Gangmu (本草綱目)
books.author: Li Shizhen (27 years of field research)
books.description: The most comprehensive pharmacopoeia in human history before the 18th century. 1,892 substances across 52 volumes.

books.title: Al-Qanun fi al-Tibb
books.author: Ibn Sina (Avicenna)
books.description: The encyclopedia that ruled Islamic and European medicine for 600 years. 760 drugs with the first systematic pharmacological classification.

books.title: Gyushi (rGyud bzhi)
books.author: Yuthok Yönten Gönpo
books.description: The foundational Tibetan medical text. 300 chapters synthesizing Indian, Chinese, and indigenous Tibetan pharmacological traditions.

books.title: Shennong Bencaojing (神農本草經)
books.author: Attributed to Shennong
books.description: The foundational Chinese materia medica. 365 substances in three therapeutic grades. Basis of Kampo (Japanese) medicine.

books.title: Dongui Bogam (동의보감)
books.author: Heo Jun — Royal physician
books.description: UNESCO Memory of the World. 25 volumes, 1,400 medicines. The most comprehensive East Asian medical encyclopedia after the Bencao Gangmu.

books.title: Historia del Nuevo Mundo
books.author: Bernabé Cobo — Jesuit missionary
books.description: The most comprehensive natural history of the Americas. 2,000+ plants from Peru, Bolivia, and Mexico — 61 years of field observation.

books.title: West African Traditional Medicine
books.author: Traditional healers across West Africa
books.description: The plant pharmacopoeia of West African traditional medicine, documented across Ghana, Nigeria, Senegal, and Côte d'Ivoire.

books.title: Southern African Traditional Medicine
books.author: San, Zulu, and Khoikhoi healers
books.description: The world's oldest continuous healing tradition from the San, who have occupied southern Africa for 40,000+ years. Source of Devil's Claw, Umckaloabo, and Rooibos.

books.title: Kampo Medicine
books.author: Tao Hongjing compilation
books.description: Japanese adaptation of the Shennong pharmacopoeia. 365 substances across three grades of medicine.

books.title: Yamato Honzo
books.author: Kaibara Ekiken
books.description: Definitive Japanese encyclopedia of natural history. 1,362 plants documented in the Edo tradition.

books.title: Maya Traditional Medicine
books.author: Indigenous Maya physicians
books.description: Mesoamerican plant medicine of the Maya civilization, preserved in colonial-era manuscripts.

books.title: Persian Zoroastrian Medicine
books.author: Avestan physicians
books.description: Zoroastrian botanical medicine bridging ancient Mesopotamia and Arabic pharmacology.

books.title: North American Indigenous Medicine
books.author: Indigenous North American healers
books.description: Native American plant medicine across hundreds of nations spanning the continent.

books.title: Amazonian Plant Medicine
books.author: Amazonian healers
books.description: The vast pharmacopoeia of the Amazon basin including ayahuasca, curare, and cat's claw.

books.title: Celtic and Norse Medicine
books.author: Celtic and Norse healers
books.description: Plant medicine of the Celtic and Norse peoples preserved in Anglo-Saxon leechbooks.

books.title: Philippine Traditional Medicine
books.author: Filipino healers
books.description: Traditional Filipino plant medicine blending Malay, Chinese, and Spanish influences.

books.title: Australian Aboriginal Medicine
books.author: Aboriginal Australian healers
books.description: 65,000 years of botanical knowledge including tea tree, eucalyptus, and bush medicines.

books.title: East African Traditional Medicine
books.author: Ethiopian and East African healers
books.description: Traditional medicine of Ethiopia, Kenya, and the Horn of Africa.

books.title: WHO Monographs on Selected Medicinal Plants
books.author: World Health Organization
books.description: 94 monographs bridging traditional plant medicine and modern pharmacology. Volumes 1-4.

books.title: German Commission E Monographs
books.author: German Federal Institute for Drugs and Medical Devices
books.description: The most rigorous evidence-based herbal medicine reference in the world. Official therapeutic monographs from Germany covering 380 herbs — the global standard for botanical medicine safety and efficacy.

books.title: American Herbal Pharmacopoeia
books.author: American Herbal Pharmacopoeia
books.description: Peer-reviewed botanical monographs covering identity, purity, quality and therapeutic application. The American standard for herbal medicine quality control.

books.title: Dongui Bogam Manuscript (東醫寶鑑)
books.author: Heo Jun 許浚
books.description: Complete 1613 original edition — National Treasure No.1085, UNESCO Memory of the World. 25 volumes of manuscript scans from the National Library of Korea, covering internal medicine, external medicine, herbal remedies, and acupuncture.

books.title: Bald's Leechbook (Royal MS 12 D XVII)
books.author: Bald and Cild (Winchester scriptorium)
books.description: England's oldest medical compendium. Contains a recipe recently proven to combat MRSA superbug. Compiled c.950 CE at Winchester from Roman, Byzantine and native Anglo-Saxon sources. 279 pages of the original manuscript now digitized at the British Library.

books.title: Leechdoms, Wortcunning & Starcraft (Cockayne 1864)
books.author: Bald (orig.) / Thomas Cockayne (trans.)
books.description: Cockayne's landmark 1864 bilingual edition of Anglo-Saxon medical texts — Old English original beside English translation. Contains Bald's Leechbook, the Old English Herbarium, and the Lacnunga charm collection.

books.title: Erbario (Italian Herbal Manuscript)
books.author: Unknown Northern Italian physician
books.description: 180 botanical illustrations in three distinct styles. Human-faced mandrake roots prescribed as anesthetics and aphrodisiacs. Written in Latin and Veneto dialect — Northern Italy, c.1400 CE. The bridge between medieval manuscript tradition and Renaissance botanical science.

books.title: Matthioli Dioscorides — Libri cinque (1544)
books.author: Pietro Andrea Matthioli
books.description: Matthioli's 1544 Italian translation of Dioscorides — the first vernacular edition of De Materia Medica. Made classical Greek botanical medicine accessible across Europe. 448 pages with woodcut illustrations. The most influential herbal of the Renaissance.

books.title: Meddygon Myddfai (Physicians of Myddfai)
books.author: Rhiwallon and his sons (Myddfai, Carmarthenshire)
books.description: The oldest surviving Welsh herbal medicine manuscript. Compiled by the hereditary physicians of Myddfai, Carmarthenshire, Wales, from the 13th century. Blends Celtic, Druidic, and Christian healing traditions.

books.title: Russian Travnik (Monastery Herbal Tradition)
books.author: Orthodox monastery physicians
books.description: Russian Orthodox monastery herbal medicine preserved in handwritten Travnik manuscripts. Blends Byzantine medical learning, Central Asian influences, and native Siberian plant knowledge — vodka, chaga, sea buckthorn, and Siberian ginseng among the defining remedies.

books.title: Yamato Honzo (大和本草) — Kaibara Ekiken
books.author: Kaibara Ekiken (貝原益軒)
books.description: The foundational encyclopedia of Japanese natural history. Kaibara Ekiken documented 1,362 plant species adapting Chinese materia medica to the Japanese context — distinguishing Japanese from Chinese plants for the first time. Pioneer of Japanese botanical medicine.

books.title: Norse & Scandinavian Plant Medicine
books.author: Anglo-Saxon and Norse healers / Völvas
books.description: Plant medicine of the Viking Age. Sources: Nine Herb Charm (invokes Odin, c.1000 CE), Henrik Harpestraeng Liber Herbarum (c.1244, oldest Danish medical text), Icelandic manuscripts (AM 434a), and archaeological plant finds from Viking burial sites.

books.title: MS XVII.J.28 — Czech Herbal & Macer Floridus
books.author: Zikmund Albík of Uničov & Odo of Meung (attrib.)
books.source: National Library of the Czech Republic, Prague
books.description: 15th-century Czech medical compendium containing the only surviving Czech translation of De viribus herbarum (Macer Floridus), a landmark medieval plant medicine text attributed to Odo of Meung, alongside a previously unknown copy of medical advice written by court physician Zikmund Albík for Holy Roman Emperor Sigismund. 226 folios, digitized by Manuscriptorium.

books.title: The Herball, or Generall Historie of Plantes
books.author: John Gerard
books.description: The foundational English-language herbal — 1,484 plants with woodcut illustrations, the first comprehensive survey of plant medicine in English.

books.title: Culpeper's English Physician and Complete Herbal
books.author: Nicholas Culpeper
books.description: Still in print after 370 years. Democratized plant medicine by writing in English rather than Latin, with planetary signatures for each plant.

books.title: King's American Dispensatory
books.author: Harvey Felter & John Uri Lloyd
books.description: The Eclectic physicians' definitive reference — 900+ plant monographs with clinical dosage, therapeutic indications, and specific symptom pictures.

books.title: American Materia Medica, Therapeutics and Pharmacognosy
books.author: Finley Ellingwood
books.description: The Eclectic clinical companion — emphasizes therapeutic indications, specific symptom pictures, and dosage. Contains the first systematic clinical documentation of Echinacea.

books.title: Theatrum Botanicum: The Theater of Plants
books.author: John Parkinson
books.description: The largest English herbal ever written — 3,800 plants by the Royal Botanist to Charles I, the definitive 17th-century English plant medicine reference.

books.title: De Historia Stirpium Commentarii Insignes
books.author: Leonhart Fuchs
books.description: The German herbal that set the standard for all European botanical illustration — 400 plants with woodcuts of unprecedented accuracy, the template that Gerard, Matthioli and Dodoens all followed.

books.title: Physica (Liber Subtilitatum)
books.author: Hildegard of Bingen
books.description: The first major European botanical work by a woman — and the most influential. Hildegard's 12th-century synthesis of plant medicine, mysticism, and the concept of viriditas (the greening power of creation) remains foundational to European herbalism.

books.title: Compendium on Simple Medicaments and Foods
books.author: Ibn al-Baytar (ابن البيطار)
books.description: The largest medieval pharmacopoeia ever written — 1,400 plant, animal, and mineral remedies compiled by the greatest Arab botanist, drawing on Greek, Arabic, and North African sources. Ibn al-Baytar traveled from Andalusia to Syria documenting every plant he encountered.

books.title: Kitab al-Jami li-Mufradat al-Adwiya wa-al-Aghdhiya
books.author: Ibn al-Baytar (d. 1248 CE)
books.description: The largest medieval pharmacopoeia ever written — 1,400 medicinal plants, animals, and minerals documented by the Andalusian botanist and chief herbalist to Sultan al-Kamil of Egypt. Synthesizes Dioscorides, Avicenna, and centuries of Islamic botanical knowledge.

books.title: Florentine Codex, Book XI — Natural Things
books.author: Bernardino de Sahagún with Nahua scribe-artists
books.description: Book XI of Sahagún's General History of the Things of New Spain: the Nahua natural history of plants, animals and minerals, including the medicinal herbs of central Mexico, in parallel Nahuatl and Spanish columns with painted illustrations. Every page transcribed and translated into English.

books.title: Honzō Zufu (本草圖譜) — Illustrated Manual of Medicinal Plants
books.author: Iwasaki Tsunemasa (Kan’en)
books.description: The largest illustrated botanical work of Edo Japan: hand-painted plates of medicinal plants drawn from life, arranged by the categories of Li Shizhen's Bencao Gangmu, with names and notes in kanji and kana.

books.title: Honzō Wamyō (本草和名)
books.author: Fukae Sukehito
books.description: Japan's earliest surviving materia medica dictionary: about a thousand Chinese drug names matched to their Japanese equivalents, the bridge through which Chinese pharmacy entered Japan.

books.title: MS XVII.G.9 — Bohemian Medical Compendium
books.author: National Library of the Czech Republic
books.description: A Latin medical compendium from 15th-century Bohemia, joining the theoretical medicine of Charles University with practical herbal recipes.

books.title: MS XVI.F.2 — Prager Wundarznei
books.author: National Library of the Czech Republic
books.description: Prague surgical medicine in the German vernacular: wounds, fractures, skin diseases and their plant-based salves and plasters.

books.title: MS VI.F.7 — Astronomical & Medical Miscellany
books.author: National Library of the Czech Republic
books.description: A Bohemian miscellany where astronomical tables and astrological prognostication sit beside medical recipes: the medieval medicine of the heavens and the herb garden together.
